evidence: Ov. Met. 3.590–591: nīl ille relīquit praeter aquās

terms.gloss: except, but (after a negative: nothing but, no one but)
terms.grammar: conjunction; the word excepted keeps the case of the word it is taken from
evidence: Sen. Ep. 123.1: nihil habeō parātī nisi mē
Quint. 6 pr. 14: nēmō nisi suā culpā diū dolet
terms.comment: After a negative or a question: nihil nisi, nothing but.

phrases.latin: cum trāderet artem, ‘accipe quās habeō, studiī successor et hērēs,’ dīxit ‘opēs.’ moriēnsque mihi nīl ille relīquit praeter aquās
phrases.english: when he handed on his craft, he said, “Take the wealth I have, my successor and heir in the trade”; and when he died he left me nothing but the waters

phrases.latin: omnia habuimus praeter tē; oculī enim meī hīc erant
phrases.english: we had everything except you; my eyes kept turning this way

phrases.latin: ‘at sī stāret’ ait ‘caelebs sine palmite truncus, nīl praeter frondēs, quārē peterētur, habēret’
phrases.english: “But if the trunk stood alone, without its vine,” she said, “it would have nothing but leaves to make anyone want it”

phrases.latin: itinere cōnfectus incommodō magis quam longō in Albānum meum multā nocte pervēnī: nihil habeō parātī nisi mē
phrases.english: worn out by a journey more awkward than long, I reached my house at Alba late at night: nothing is ready except me

phrases.latin: tōta mihi dormītur hiems et pinguior illō tempore sum quō mē nīl nisi somnus alit
phrases.english: I sleep the whole winter through, and I am fattest at the time when nothing but sleep feeds me

phrases.latin: nūlla jam ultrā gēns, nihil nisi flūctūs et saxa
phrases.english: there is no people beyond us now, nothing but waves and rocks

sources: Lewis & Short: praeter · Lewis & Short: nisi
